main_text.p: ætum[?], vereor ut mox oraculum, uti sunt mores. At ipsi viderint. ego de me testor, pacis mihi ingenium esse, & cum Hesiodo,
Μηδὲ κακῶν ἑταίρων μηδ' ἐχθρὸν νικητῆρα[?]:

& in hoc ipso sermone bellico, nihil tamen spirare bellicum. Tu Deus, qui Pax & Amor es, da consentire & conspirare in commune bonum: da te, virtutes, honesta studia amare: & hæc iuuare pro viribus & copia, quam dedisti aut dabis. Nos quid sumus? humiles, imo humus: tu super omnes, tu omnia: & à te, quidquid boni est, Summo bono. Hoc ama, me dilige mi AVDI-TOR, & vale. Avd. O tu quoque longum mi doctor, mi parens, nec aliter te appellem.
main_text.head: BREVIARIVM LIBRI VLTIMI.

l.i: Prætoris, Quæstoris, Legatorum, Tribunorum, & Militum metatura.
Munia. quæ continent Ministeria, Excubias, Circuitiones, & alia in castris.
Exercitia. quæ sunt Oneris, vt in Agmine (& per occasionem Agmen descriptum:) aut Operis, aut denique Armorum.
Leges. quæ variæ sunt. nos e Polybio explicauimus eas quæ tangunt Furta, Stipendia, Præmia, Pœnas, Missionem.
In clausula, Comparata militia nostra cum prisca.

page.notes: The strip of text at the far left edge belongs to the neighbouring page and is left out. The Greek verse line and the Latin verse line are read from the scan; the Greek ends in [?] and the Latin "bonisue" is doubtful. The tail of the first word of the page ("ætum") is partly hidden at the top of the text block. The diagram is read as a bracketed outline: the label "Disciplinæ sedes sunt" opens two groups, and "Partes sunt" opens the three groups below it.
